headline_read: WHICH OCCUPATIONS MAKE THE CEILINGS: Houston's $128,040 p90 vs Memphis's $100,640 p90 (both 2025 OEWS, as-published).

THE BAND ITSELF: the specialized band (~2/3-p90 mean-threshold) holds ~23-28% of jobs in EVERY metro with a similar occupation count (143-200) - the ceiling is not about MORE band jobs, it is about WHAT IS IN THE BAND and WHAT IT PAYS (band weighted-mean x p90 r=+0.98).

THE CEILING AXES across the 10 metros: Computer/Math band-share r=+0.86, Management band-share r=+0.73 (CM+Mgmt joint axis); Houston 44.6% CM+Mgmt (4th) vs Memphis 29.1% (9th); NYC 42.8, Boston 49.7, OKC 29.8, NOLA 27.6.

HOUSTON vs MEMPHIS, group deltas: Management +12.9pp (569k band jobs in Houston, wmean $146,948), Architecture/Engineering +4.5pp (57.7k jobs, $127,760 - the oil&gas engineer mass), Computer/Math +2.6pp, Science +2.0pp; Memphis carries the logistics mass in the OPPOSITE direction (Transport band-share +2.7pp over Houston, wmean $71,465 - First-Line Supervisors of Transportation at $68-74k, not pilots), and Office/Admin +6.3pp in ITS band.

MEMPHIS'S LOWEST-P10-HIGH-P90-TAIL: its ceiling is held by healthcare + a thin management layer: top mass = Registered Nurses 13,760 @ $87,370, Gen&Ops Managers 9,730 @ $132,440, first-line supervisors (office + transportation) ~13,200 @ $68-74k; the only $150k+ wmeans in the band are Legal ($156,726) and healthcare practitioners' mean $113,384.

THE HOUSTON WAGE-PREMIUM INSIDE SHARED GROUPS: same occupations pay ~10-15% more in Houston's band (Business/Financial wmean $101,463 vs $85,157; HC-Pract $125,691 vs $113,384; Arch/Eng $127,760 vs $98,666; Computer/Math $119,519 vs $103,044) - the p90 gap is BOTH mix (what jobs) AND level (what each pays).

MASS-SIDE TRUTH: Houston's ceiling rests on 97,320 General & Operations Managers ($146,320) + 65,910 RNs ($100,290) + 35,550 PM Specialists + 28,400 Accountants + 22,940 Software Developers ($133,130); Memphis's equivalent layer is 1/5 the size (13,760 RNs + 9,730 G&OMs).
NATIONAL frame: national specialized band = 313 occs, 95.9M jobs (61.7% of US employment at the 2/3-p90 mean threshold), wmean $124,751 vs national p90 $128,560.
